test.name: User declines the current plan item: skip it as user_declined and do not run it
test.description: An active plan's current item (pli_001, sequence 1) is a probate search; the user's message declines it and asks for the census item instead. The declined item must be set `skipped` with `skip_category: "user_declined"` and a `skip_reason` — a decline is terminal — and no search may be run or logged for it. Graded deterministically by test_user_declined_item_skipped_not_searched. Issue #2213 PR 3 item 1.

input.user_message: I don't want to spend time on the probate search for Elias - leave the estate files out of this. Go ahead with the 1880 census search in the plan.

judge_context: CORE: the user declined pli_001 (the probate search). Correct behaviour is to set pli_001 `skipped` with `skip_category: "user_declined"` and a short `skip_reason` naming the user's decline, run no search for it, and then execute pli_002 (the 1880 census) as asked. Whether pli_001 was skipped correctly and left unsearched is decided by a deterministic validator — do not re-grade it, and do not deduct on any dimension for it.
Do NOT penalise the skill for not offering to run the probate search later, and do NOT penalise it for not proposing a replacement probate strategy: the user declined it.
Completeness: the census search executed, logged, its plan item updated, and the hit reported is complete. Do NOT require extraction.

The census `wiki_read` from Step 2's pre-work block is NOT graded on Tool Arguments — score that dimension on the `record_search` call's arguments. The census fixture's predicate matches any URL containing `United_States_Census`, so a per-year page is answered by the same country page; that is the shape of the fixture set, not a wrong call.
